findings.title: The NIR beam passes visibly through a solid bookshelf inside the glass lab (clutter sits in the beam corridor)
findings.problem: The clutter `shelf` recipe puts a full bookshelf just inside the lab, right on the line from the hatch to the lab pad. The scene dump gives its posts at x 4.31/6.23 and z −4.33/−4.70, so it is centred at about (5.27, −4.51), 2.0 × 0.45 m, with 6×3 coloured book blocks. Delivery 2 traces the beam from the hatch midpoint (5.4, −3.2) to the lab pad (7, −6). At z = −4.5 that line is at x ≈ 6.14, inside the shelf's x span of 4.27–6.27. The beam is a pure plan-ray against `walls()` (src/stations/spectrum/logic.ts:110-127) and ignores props, so the pink beam is drawn straight through the books (shots 70, 71, 72). This is the one room whose lesson is "what an obstacle does depends on the band", and a solid wooden bookshelf letting near-IR straight through contradicts the shutter and brick next to it. It also reads as an obvious render bug: a glowing line through solid geometry. The level's clutter lanes (src/levels/spectrum.ts:34-37) protect walking routes, but not the beam corridors from the hatch to the pad, from mirror A to the hatch, or through smoke to the quiet room.
findings.fix: In src/levels/spectrum.ts `clutter.lanes`, add beam-corridor lanes so clutter is never seeded on a taught beam path: {points:[[5.4,-3.3],[7,-6]],r:.9} (hatch to lab pad), {points:[[-.4,2.3],[3.56,0.01],[5.4,-3.2]],r:.7} (tower to mirror A to hatch), {points:[[-.4,2.3],[1,5.8],[8.2,4.8]],r:.7} (C-mirror and quiet room legs), and {points:[[-.4,2.3],[-8.2,-5.8]],r:.6} (storeroom radio leg, for clarity). Better still, derive the lanes from logic.ts (TX, SPOTS, PADS, HATCH) so they can't drift. Optionally make legHits() in logic.ts treat any prop with mass ≥ 9 standing in the leg as a 'wood' hit, so a knocked-over shelf is a real obstacle.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/s6-solve2.mjs. Shots 70/71 must show the pink beam reaching the lab pad without crossing any prop. Add a unit check in src/stations/spectrum/logic.test.ts (or a clutter test) that no clutter PropSpec footprint intersects the segments hatchMid→PADS.lab and TX→SPOTS.A for seed 7.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this myself. I placed a mirror on mark A, set NIR, aimed tx→A and A→lab, and opened the hatch. The pink beam runs straight through the clutter bookshelf inside the lab (verify-spectrum-models-06-lab-beam-vs-shelf-z9.jpg); shots 70, 71 and 72 show the same. The scene dump puts the shelf at (5.27,-4.51), 2.0×0.45 m, boards at y .27/.87/1.47, under 1.8 m tall. The beam leg (hatch mid (5.4,-3.2) → lab pad (7,-6)) crosses z −4.51 at x ≈ 6.15, inside the shelf's x span 4.27–6.27, at BEAM_Y 1.25 (station.ts:22). legHits (logic.ts:120-127) tests only walls() and SMOKE, so props never block the beam. Clutter lanes (spectrum.ts:35-38) cover walking routes only. P1 stands: this is the taught beam of delivery 2, seen at the game camera (72), and it contradicts the lesson.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/scene.json: bookshelf boards 2×0.06×0.45 at (5.27,{.27,.87,1.47},-4.51); some of the books are #ffc94d
src/levels/clutter.ts:42 (shelf recipe = bookshelf + box + bin), :80 (lane test)
findings.fix_correction: The lane part is right: clutter.ts:80 rejects any item within lane r + rad*.7, so beam-corridor lanes will keep clutter off the beams. Drop the optional 'legHits treats props with mass ≥ 9 as wood' idea. logic.ts is pure, unit-tested plan geometry. Making links depend on loose props would let a knocked-over prop break the clean solution, which goes against 'never fail for chaos'. If anything, keep it to visuals: tint the beam where it passes a prop, or keep heavy clutter out of the lab corridor entirely.

findings.title: Job items don't carry the job-yellow language, while yellow clutter crowds the pod
findings.problem: DR-45 says job items share one yellow language (#ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes) and no decorative clutter uses it. Spectrum inverts this. The two carry-and-place job items, the RX pod (coolbox #fbf3e2 with a teal lid) and the mirror boards (#dfe8f0 with a lilac rail), contain no job yellow. Meanwhile three non-job props use it: a #ffc94d office chair beside the desk (src/levels/spectrum.ts:18, x −4.4 z 4.6), a #ffc94d box by the entrance (:20, x −8.7 z 7.1), and #ffd66b crates from the clutter palette (:34 colors[1]). Two yellow crates sit right against the pod dock in the start and dock shots (01, 13, 52). The storeroom door knob and the tea mug are also #ffc94d. A first-time player scanning for 'the yellow thing' finds a chair and boxes. The pod is cream on a cream floor (norim luma 178 vs floor 207), so it relies only on its teal lid to stand out.
findings.fix: (1) In src/levels/spectrum.ts, recolour the chair at (−4.4,4.6) to '#5b9cf0' and the box at (−8.7,7.1) to '#c98f5a'. Replace clutter colour '#ffd66b' with '#f0a3b5' or '#9fd8c8'. (2) Give the pod the job language. In prefabs.ts `coolbox`, make the lid band and the handle '#ffc629' with two INK hazard stripes (box .04×.005×d, rotated 45°) when spec.id==='pod'. Alternatively, in station.ts setup(), add a yellow collar ring (TorusGeometry(.5,.03), '#ffc629') around the podTop mast base and make the RX POD tag '#ffc629' with INK text. (3) Give the mirror boards a '#ffc629' top rail instead of '#8b7be8' (station.ts:181) and yellow feet caps. (4) Change the storeroom knob to DMETAL (room.ts:66).
findings.verify: Retake spectrum-models-01-start and -02-survey. In a hue-mask (|ΔE| < 25 from #ffc94d), only the pod, the mirrors, the hatch frame and the grab cue/marker light up.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the claim. The pod is coolbox #fbf3e2 with lid #3bb2c9 (spectrum.ts:8, prefabs.ts:173-176). The mirrors are #dfe8f0 with a #8b7be8 rail (station.ts:181). Neither job item carries job yellow. Non-job #ffc94d shows up on the chair (spectrum.ts:18), the box (:20), the mug (room.ts:115), the storeroom knob (room.ts:68, not 66), and on clutter bookshelf books (scene.json). Clutter colours include #ffd66b (spectrum.ts:34). Shots 01 and 13 show yellow crates against the pod dock. I downgraded to P2: the objective marker floats over the pod, and the pod is the only box with a mast, so the player is not really misled. It is a DR-45 language break, not a block on understanding.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-models-13-desk-front.jpg (yellow crate beside the pod; knocked-over yellow chair)
mockups/review5/tools/spectrum-models/scene.json: bookshelf book instances colour ffc94d at (4.58..6.02,-4.51)
findings.fix_correction: The cited knob line should be room.ts:68, not 66. Also take the #ffc94d out of the clutter bookshelf book palette (the bookshelf prefab's book colours), or the hue-mask check will still fail.

findings.title: Floors and white fixtures are too bright: floor luma 209–233, tower mast only 12 luma off the floor
findings.problem: The hall floor is kitchenTiles('#f6f2ea','#e7eef5') (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:49), and the walls, desk, tower mast, pod body, tea counter and exhibit case are all cream or paper. Measured median luma: hall floor in the start shot 209 (crop 1230,420–1330,480), survey floor 219 and 230, desk front 236. With ?norim the tower mast (PAPER) is 224 against floor 212, only 12 luma apart (DR-54 needs ≥ 25), and the blue-white crate is 159 vs 186. DR-54 targets floor luma 140–185. The result is the bleached, low-contrast hall seen in every shot. The tower, the room's main fixture, dissolves into the floor at the game camera (99b), and with lab window light the lab is near white (42, 43).
findings.fix: In room.ts:49 drop the hall tile to a mid warm grey-cream pair such as TX.kitchenTiles('#d9d2c4','#cdd5dc',6). Lab lino (:51) becomes '#c9dbe8','#b8cfe0'. Keep the walls CREAM so the wall/floor pair separates. Give the tower mast a stronger value: mast toon('#8fa3c0') with PAPER only on the turret, plus a '#3fae6a' band at the top. Make the tower base DMETAL with an INK rim instead of a solid INK disc (see the tower finding). Also lower the spectrum mood rig's hemisphere intensity (0.76) by about 15%.
findings.verify: PIL median-luma on floor crops of spectrum-models-01-start and -02-survey must be 140–185. A ?norim crop of the tower mast vs the adjacent floor must differ by ≥ 25 luma.
findings.verify_reason: I measured it myself with PIL. Floor median luma is 209 in 01-start (1230,420–1330,480) and 233 in the 02-survey centre, against a DR-54 target of 140–185. In 90-norim the tower mast is about 224 against an adjacent floor of 212: 12 luma, below the required 25. Code: hall tiles are kitchenTiles('#f6f2ea','#e7eef5') (room.ts:49), the lab is #eaf4fb/#d3e6f3 (:51), the mast is PAPER #fffdf8 (station.ts:149), and the hemisphere light is 0.76 (scene.json). DR-54 lists bright floors as P1.
extra_evidence: PIL: 01-start floor 209, 02-survey floor 233, 90-norim floor 209; mast column pixels in 90-norim ≈ 222–226 vs floor 212

findings.title: Room is under-dressed: 82 props on 22×16 m, a thin centre and a bare front-right hall
findings.problem: snap() at start reports 82 props: 37 hand-placed (src/levels/spectrum.ts:7-25) and about 45 from clutter, though `max` is 220. DR-67 scales to about 137 props for 352 m², and each walkable 4×4 m cell needs ≥ 3 props. The survey shows the whole centre empty: the band from the tower to the lab shutter (x 0…5, z −1…2), the hall between mirror marks A and B, and the strip in front of the quiet room. The clutter lanes are r = 1.0 and blanket almost the whole floor (8 polylines at spectrum.ts:35-37), and step 2.1 then leaves few legal cells. The clutter that is placed repeats the same kraft/pink/blue crate trio along the front stripes (01, 02, 59). The storeroom shelf stock is ten identical rounded blocks (room.ts:73-74). AGENTS 3 (big, dense rooms with hundreds of props) is not met.
findings.fix: (1) Narrow the walking lanes to r .8 and keep them off the hall centre, where the beams are covered by their own corridors (see the beam finding). (2) Add themed clusters at fixed spots off the routes: a 'research cart' at (2.6,-1.2) (cart + 2 boxes + paper); an 'instrument table' at (−1.8,0.4) (desk variant + monitor + mug, rotated 0.3); a spare-mirror rack against the x = −11 wall at z ≈ 0 (two leaning whiteboard frames without glass, visibly different from the job mirrors); a coat-stand + plant + bin corner at (4.6,7.2). (3) Add recipes 'reading' and 'plants' to the spectrum recipe list so no recipe exceeds 25%. Change `fill` to include 'bins' and 'cones'. (4) Vary the shelf stock: alternate box sizes .3/.42/.24, add binders (box .06×.3×.24 in desaturated book colours) and a few cylinders (paint tins).
findings.verify: snap().props ≥ 130. A heat-map of snap().items plus prop positions shows every walkable 4×4 m cell with ≥ 3 props. The survey (spectrum-models-02-survey) has no bare floor patch larger than 3×3 m outside the marked beam corridors, and tests/routes or the spectrum spec still pass with no extra detour.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the count: snap().props = 82 at start (v1.mjs and v2-dc.mjs). Counting spectrum.ts:8-24 gives exactly 37 hand-placed props, so about 45 come from clutter, well under max 220. Nine lane polylines at r=1 (spectrum.ts:35-38) cover most of the hall. The 02 and A5 surveys and 65 show the empty centre band between the tower, mark A and the lab shutter. The storeroom stock is 10 identical rbox blocks (room.ts:73-74). DR-67 scales to roughly 137 props for 352 m², so AGENTS 3 is not met.
findings.fix_correction: r .8 keeps the lanes 1.6 m wide, which satisfies DR-16 (1.2 m lanes need only r .6). Re-run the spec route to confirm there is no added detour. Note there are 9 lane polylines, not 8. Add the beam corridors from finding 0 at the same time so the new clusters don't land on a beam.

findings.title: Transmitter tower: the colour band rings are buried inside the mast; the silhouette reads as a glove on a stick
findings.problem: The tower is the room's central machine (src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:149-153). Its mast is cyl(.07,.09,1.1), which is 0.0855 m radius at y .35 and 0.0805 at y .63. The five band rings are cyl(.075,.075,.04), smaller than the mast at every height, so all five rings are entirely inside the mast and never render. No band colour shows on the tower in any shot (B0, B1, 15). What remains is a white tapering pole on a large solid-INK disc (r .46) that reads as a hole in the floor, plus a plain white rounded box turret with two hairline antennas (r .01). At the game camera this reads as a white glove raising two fingers, or a toothbrush (99b), not a transmitter. It has fewer than 6 distinguishing cues (DR-62) and no cable or conduit to the desk, although it is 'the tower by the desk'. The back of the turret is a blank box.
findings.fix: In station.ts buildHall(): change the rings to cyl(.105,.105,.045,20) at y .32+i*.075, or better torus rings TorusGeometry(.095,.022,8,24) rotated flat. Replace the INK base with a two-step plinth: cyl(.42,.46,.08) DMETAL plus cyl(.3,.34,.06) '#6b7385' with four bolt heads (sphere .025, INK). Add a lattice: three diagonal box(.03,.5,.03) braces at 120° from the plinth to the mast at y .6. On the turret add a horn or dish emitter (cyl(.06,.13,.16,18,'z') glossy '#dfe3ea' at z .26), an INK vent grille plane on the back (3 box slats), and thicken the antennas to r .018 with ball tips (sphere .03 in the current band colour). Run a floor cable tray from the desk's right end (−1.3,3.0) to the plinth: box(1.2,.04,.12) DMETAL with an INK cable on top. That also gives the room a visible cable (DR-05).
findings.verify: Retake shots B0/B1 (s10-tower.mjs) and the start shot. All five band rings are visible at zoom 9, the tower names as 'a transmitter' in the squint test on the norim start shot, and a turret back view (B2) shows a finished vent.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry checks out. The mast is CylinderGeometry(rt .07, rb .09, h 1.1) centred at y .65 (kit.ts:28, station.ts:149), so its radius is .0855 at y .35 and .0804 at y .63. Every ring is cyl(.075,.075,.04) at y .35+i*.07 (station.ts:150), smaller than the mast at its height, so all five rings sit inside it. My zoom-9 shot shows a plain white mast on a black disc with no colour bands (verify-spectrum-models-01-tower-z9.jpg), matching B0 and 99b. The turret is a plain rbox with two antennas of r .01 (station.ts:151-152).
findings.fix_correction: A decorative floor cable tray does not satisfy DR-05. That rule is about a physical cable act in the job, so drop that justification; the tray is fine as dressing. The ring change is enough on its own: cyl(.1,.1,.045) at the same heights clears the mast, whose radius is at most .09.

findings.title: The pod is carried at head height beside Pip's face, its detector mast towers over the hat, and the mirrors are carried upright beside the head
findings.problem: The carry target for light props is y = p.y + .55, 1.05 m ahead (src/game.ts:331), independent of prop height. The pod (coolbox, 1.0×0.6×0.65, mass 6) therefore rides with its lid at Pip's head height, offset to his side in most views, held up by one mitt. Its podTop mast and green detector head rise about 0.5 m above the hard hat (51b, 52, 53b). From the default camera the pod covers Pip's face and right arm (50). The whiteboard-based mirror (1.7 m tall) is carried vertically beside his head, with the rail edge-on past his ear and shoulder (61). DR-65 asks for level carries in front of the chest, held by both mitts, never vertical beside the head. In this room Pip carries the pod for most of the job (three deliveries).
findings.fix: In game.ts:331, compute the light-carry height from the prop's size so its bottom sits at the waist: target.y = p.y - .1 + kind.size[1]/2 (Pip's body centre ≈ .9 gives a bottom at about .8 m). Set ahead = .45 + kind.size[2]/2 and lerp heading-aligned yaw onto the body (setRotation from this.heading) so the box faces forward between both mitts. For tall flat props (whiteboard/mirror, size[1] > 1.2) carry them low and in front, bottom at .25 m, rotated so the board is perpendicular to the heading. Pip then 'pushes' the board like a sign, and his head stays visible over it. Update pipRig carry arm pose (rig.update carrying) to reach to the new height.
findings.verify: Rerun s5-solve.mjs: in shots 51/52/53 the pod's bounding box doesn't intersect a 0.3 m sphere at Pip's head (y ≈ 1.4), and both mitts touch the pod sides. In shot 61 the mirror is in front of Pip, below chin height.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:331 carries light props (mass < 15) at y = p.y+.55, 1.05 m ahead, whatever their size. The coolbox is 1.0×0.6×0.65, mass 6, and the whiteboard 1.7×1.7×0.2, mass 9 (prefabs.ts:18,24). In 52 the pod rides beside Pip's face with the mast above the hat. In 61 the mirror is carried upright and edge-on beside his head. This breaks DR-65.
extra_evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:18 whiteboard size [1.7,1.7,.2] mass 9; :24 coolbox [1.0,.6,.65] mass 6
findings.fix_correction: The mirror part of the fix is wrong. A 1.7 m board carried perpendicular to the heading with its bottom at .25 m reaches 1.95 m, above Pip's head (about 1.4–1.6). It would hide his whole body from the default camera behind him, so his head would not 'stay visible over it'. Instead, carry tall flat boards edge-on (board plane parallel to the heading), low in front of the chest with the bottom near .3 m. Or tilt them to lie flat like a tray at waist height. For the pod, target.y = p.y - .1 + size[1]/2 is reasonable (p.y ≈ .77 is the capsule centre).

findings.title: Pod reads as an arcade joystick, and its lid handle runs into the mast plate
findings.problem: The receiver pod is a coolbox prefab with a podTop overlay (src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:172-175). The overlay is a thin grey mast (cyl .03) on an INK plate, topped with a green dome on a black cylinder (visdiode head ×1.5). At the game camera (99c) and at zoom 9 this is exactly an arcade joystick's ball-top lever on a box. The arcade room teaches with real arcade cabinets, so a player is primed to read 'joystick' here. The detector heads that are supposed to change per band read as slight variations of the same knob. The coolbox's curved carry handle, Torus(.13) centred at x 0 (src/props/prefabs.ts:176), spans x −0.13…+0.13 on the lid. The podTop INK plate rbox(.36,.05,.3) at x .2 spans x .02….38, so the handle's right foot sinks into the plate (visible in 51b and 53b). The white latch at x −.28 (prefabs.ts:175) also sits in front of the left end of the 'RX POD' tag (tag at z .331, latch to z .36).
findings.fix: (1) Move the podTop mast and plate to x .28 and shrink the plate to rbox(.24,.05,.24) so it clears the handle (handle ends at .13 + .02 tube). Or rotate the coolbox handle 90° to run front-to-back at x −.25. (2) Make the detector read as a sensor, not a knob: put each head on a short yoke (two DMETAL box(.02,.12,.02) uprights with a cross pin) tilted 20° toward the tower, and give the heads distinct silhouettes at 1.5×. Dipole: two longer white rods (.32 each) on a horizontal bar. Patch: a 0.24 square copper tile on a tilted plate. Thermopile: a gold horn. Diodes: a lens dome inside a short INK hood (cyl .07, open front). (3) Put the RX POD tag on the front lid band (y .2) or move the latches to y .26 so they don't overlap it. (4) Add a small aerial-style status lamp ring around the mast base (it lights when the band matches) to show state on the device (DR-47).
findings.verify: Retake crops 99c and 51b. No geometry intersects the handle. The squint test on the norim start shot names the pod as 'a receiver/sensor box', not a joystick. Each band's head is distinguishable in a side-by-side of five g.act('band',b) zoom-9 crops.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry checks out. The coolbox handle is a half Torus(.13,.02) at x 0, y h/2+.04 = .34 (prefabs.ts:176). Its right foot (x .11–.15, y .34) sits inside the podTop INK plate rbox(.36,.05,.3) at x .2, y .32, which spans x .02–.38 and y .295–.345 (station.ts:172). The left latch box(.14,.08,.03) at x −.28, y .108, z .33–.36 (prefabs.ts:175) overlaps the top-left of the RX POD tag plane (x −.37..+.13, y −.06..+.10, z .331; station.ts:175). In 99c and 51b the handle visibly runs into the plate, and the mast on its black plate with the green dome reads as an arcade joystick.

findings.title: Floating, single-sided sign planes (TEA, POD DOCK, QUIET ROOM, HATCH, GLASS LAB); the QUIET ROOM sign is invisible from the approach side
findings.problem: Every room sign is `standingSign()` (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:35-37): a bare PlaneGeometry with a MeshBasic texture, front side only, no housing and no post. (1) 'TEA' (room.ts:116) hangs in mid-air at y 1.5, z 5.2, 0.35 m in front of the counter's front face (z 5.16) and 0.55 m above its top, with no support (18, B0). (2) 'POD DOCK' (:133) is a 0.8 m plate standing on edge on the rug at y .35 with no foot, so it reads as a loose sheet leaning on nothing (13, 99c). (3) 'QUIET ROOM · SCREENED' (:106) faces +z, into the quiet room. The player approaches from the lab side (z < 1.5, route via 10.2,0.6), where the sign is back-face-culled and invisible (97); it is only readable from inside the room (23). (4) 'HATCH' and 'GLASS LAB' (:92-93) float 5 cm off the shutter face (shutter front at z1+.05, sign at z1+.10), against DR-72's 0.5–1 cm. When the hatch door slides up 0.62 m (station.ts:400), the door's front face reaches z −3.10, coplanar with the HATCH sign at y 1.75–1.89, which is a z-fight risk (66). DR-63: signs have housings, never open-backed planes.
findings.fix: Rewrite standingSign() to build a housed plaque: rbox(w+.06, h+.06, .04, .015) in the bg colour's darker shade, with the texture plane on BOTH faces at ±.021 (two planes, one rotated π), mounted 0.6 cm off the host surface. Mount each sign on something. TEA: on a 0.9 m DMETAL post (cyl .02) rising from the back of the counter at (2.4, 0.95→1.6, 4.6), or flat on the counter's front face at y .7, z 5.17. POD DOCK: lay it flat on the floor as a decal at y .013 (rotation.x = −π/2) at the dock's +z edge, like the PAD tags. QUIET ROOM: double-sided and hung from the top rail on two short chains (box .01×.12×.01), centred at y 2.05. HATCH/GLASS LAB: z = lb.z1 + .056. Put the HATCH sign at y 2.0 so the open hatch door (top at 1.87+.3) passes behind it, or move the hatch door to z1+.06 (behind the frame).
findings.verify: Orbit 180° (g.orbit(700)) around each sign at zoom 9. Every sign is visible from both sides and touches a post, rail, wall or counter. After g.act('hatch') a 0.1 s pair of zoom-9 shots on the hatch shows no flicker on the HATCH sign.
findings.verify_reason: standingSign (room.ts:35-37) is a bare PlaneGeometry with a MeshBasic material on its front side only (kit.ts:61). TEA floats at y 1.5, z 5.2, in front of and above the counter (18, and my verify-01). The HATCH sign front is at z1+.10. The hatch door (z1+.08, thickness .04) also has its front face at z1+.10, and once raised by .62 (station.ts:401) it covers y 1.57–2.17, overlapping the sign's 1.75–1.89. The faces are exactly coplanar. My open-hatch zoom-9 crop shows speckling on the sign edge, and two frames 0.1 s apart differ by 750 pixels over 30. The QUIET ROOM sign faces +z (room.ts:106), so it is culled from the north (97).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-spectrum-models-09-hatch-sign-crop.jpg (speckle on the HATCH sign with the door raised)
mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-models-02-survey.jpg (QUIET ROOM sign readable from the default camera)
findings.fix_correction: Two corrections. (a) POD DOCK is worse than described. It is centred at y .35 with height .176, so it floats about 26 cm above the floor rather than standing on the rug; the floor-decal fix is right. (b) QUIET ROOM is not invisible from the usual approach. The default camera sits at +z (yaw .14) and reads it correctly through the mesh, as 02-survey shows. It disappears only when the player orbits to the north side, so the real issue is that it is single-sided (DR-63), and it is not a readability blocker. For the hatch, moving the sign to z1+.056 is not enough while the door front is also at z1+.10. Put the door behind the frame (z1+.04) or the sign clearly in front of it (≥ z1+.11).

findings.title: Toaster smoke is a flat white veil that washes out Pip and the tea coworker, hides its own toaster, and reads as a glow from low angles
findings.problem: Fourteen billboard sprites (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:118-119, animated in station.ts:402-403) scale 0.8 → 2.7 m with opacity up to 0.5, colour #b4b8c6, depthWrite off. Near the tea corner they stack into a uniform translucent sheet. Standing at the counter turns Pip's yellow helmet near-white and veils the orange coworker and the whole counter (A8, 95, 96). The toaster (0.36×0.24×0.22 m) can't be seen as the source. From the default high camera the cloud reads as a grey smudge on the floor (02, 59). From low orbits it is a 2.5 m soft white column that looks like a lamp bloom, not burnt-toast smoke (07, 15, 17). DR-79 says smoke never stacks into a solid mass or blocks Pip. Mirror mark C and the tea-corner route (lane [.6,4.2]) both pass through it.
findings.fix: Make the smoke read as toon puffs from a visible source. Use 8 sprites, not 14. Scale 0.35 → 1.3 m (s = .35 + u*.95). Peak opacity .32, fading in over u < .15 and out from u > .6. Use a darker burnt grey '#8d8f9c' with a lighter core (TX.radial with a hard 0.55 stop for a cel edge). Start the puffs exactly at the toaster slots (2.1, 1.2, 4.85) rising 0.9 m before drifting toward SMOKE. Add a sprite-free zone: skip any puff whose screen-space footprint covers Pip (or set opacity *= .3 when within 1 m of the player). Make the toaster read: a slightly larger body rbox(.44,.28,.26), a side lever (box .04×.02×.06, INK), a coiled cord to the wall, and a faint hot-orange slot glow (hot('#ff8a3d',1.2) plane in each slot).
findings.verify: Retake A8, 95 and 17 (s9-yaws.mjs, s8-closeups.mjs). Pip's helmet keeps its yellow (median hue within 10° of #ffc94d in a helmet crop). The toaster and its slots are visible under the smoke, and the low-orbit shot shows distinct puffs rising from the toaster.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches: 14 sprites, opacity .45, depthWrite off, colour #b4b8c6 (room.ts:118-119), animated at station.ts:403. A8 shows Pip's helmet washed near-white and the counter and coworker veiled. 07 shows a white column from the low orbit. DR-79 ('never block Pip') is broken.
findings.fix_correction: The smoke is a taught obstacle: logic.SMOKE (2.4, 3.4, r 1.3) attenuates NIR and visible light. The visual cloud must still cover that disc at beam height (y ≈ 1.25), or players will see beams dimmed by invisible smoke. Shrink and thin the individual puffs, but keep them spread over the SMOKE footprint, and fade them near Pip. Don't shrink the cloud as a whole to a 1.3 m column at the toaster.

findings.title: Storeroom shelf stock reads as bread loaves: identical rounded blocks with no box cues
findings.problem: The storeroom's two shelving units (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:73-74) hold 5 stock items each: rbox(.3,.28,.34,.04) in three kraft tones, on alternate boards only, with the top board empty. The edge radius on a near-cube that small, the warm toast colours and the lack of tape, flaps or labels make them look like loaves of bread or tofu at zoom 9 and at the game camera (33, 34, 35). DR-52 explicitly bans props that read as bread. The prefab 'box' props in the same room have tape and a label and read correctly, so the shelf stock even contradicts the room's own boxes. The shelves are also lightly built: 0.06 m boards with no back panel, so from the hall over the brick wall they read as an empty frame.
findings.fix: In room.ts:73-74, replace each stock rbox with a mini box group: rbox(w,h,d,.02) kraft plus a tape strip box(w+.004,.004,.06) '#e8d6b0' across the top, plus a flap seam (box(.004,.004,d) INK at 40% opacity). Or reuse the prefab box mesh builder scaled 0.45. Vary the sizes (.26–.42) and fill all three boards (y .43, 1.13, 1.83) with 3–4 items each, including two binders (box .07×.3×.25 in books[] colours, desaturated) and a paint tin (cyl .09,.09,.14). Add a back panel box(2,1.9,.02) '#b98552' at z −.24 and a kick board.
findings.verify: Retake spectrum-models-33/34 at zoom 9. A first-look naming of the shelf contents says 'boxes/stock', and no item is the same size and colour as its neighbour.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:73-74 places 5 rbox(.3,.28,.34,.04) blocks per unit in three kraft tones, on two boards only, with no tape or labels. In 33 and 34 they read as bread loaves next to the taped prefab boxes in the same room, which DR-52 bans. The shelves have no back panel.

findings.title: Brick texture squashed on narrow wall faces; wall caps and the STOREROOM sign stay opaque when the brick wall fades
findings.problem: (1) Each brick slab gets one cloned texture with repeat (len/1.3, 1.6) (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:62) applied to every face of a box(). The 0.3 m end faces and edge returns therefore get the same horizontal repeat as the full-length face. At the storeroom's corner returns and the lab side wall, bricks come out as thin vertical slivers (34 right edge, 14 left edge). (2) The brick slabs are faded occluders (slab() pushes them into game.occluders, room.ts:39-43). The cream cap box (:70), the brown pier caps (:69) and the 'STOREROOM' sign (:71) are separate meshes that never fade. When Pip walks behind the storeroom front wall, the faded bricks show a hard cream cap bar, two brown blocks and the sign floating at full opacity over him (33). DR-78 asks for no outline ghost and no popping in front of a half-faded mesh. (3) In 14 the same wall does not fade at all while it hides Pip's body from a camera over the storeroom; only his head shows above it.
findings.fix: (1) Build brick walls as a box with per-face UVs scaled to world size: after creating box(w,h,d), rewrite the uv attribute so each face's u = face width / 1.3 and v = face height / 1.3 (a small helper worldUV(geo) in src/render/kit.ts), and set repeat to (1,1). Alternatively cap the end faces with a 0.3 m plain mortar trim box. (2) Parent the cap, pier caps and sign to the faded slab mesh, or register them in a fade group (game.occluders entries that share opacity with their wall: e.g. slab returns the mesh, and `fadeWith(mesh, ...children)`). Their materials need transparent:true. (3) For DR-12, add the chest and head rays (p.y+.9, p.y+1.5) to the occlusion test in src/game.ts:386-388 so a 2.1 m wall between the camera and Pip's torso fades.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 shots at the storeroom corners show bricks with the same aspect on long and short faces. Rerun s3-back.mjs shot 33: cap, caps and sign fade together with the bricks. Retake 14: Pip's torso is visible through a faded wall.
findings.verify_reason: (1) room.ts:62 sets repeat (len/1.3, 1.6) on one texture shared by every box face, and the 0.3 m return faces show squashed vertical brick slivers (34, right pier). (2) slab() pushes only the slab mesh into game.occluders (room.ts:41). The cap (:70), pier caps (:69) and STOREROOM sign (:71) are separate, unfaded meshes, and in 33 they sit at full opacity over a faded wall with Pip behind it. (3) game.ts:387 casts a single ray to p.y+.4. In 14, and in 61 (the lab side slab with its orange cap), Pip's torso is hidden behind an unfaded 2.1 m wall. In 14 the dispatch desk also stands in the line of sight.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-models-61-carry-mirror-zoom9-side.jpg (lab side wall, room.ts:77, hides Pip's body unfaded)

findings.title: Big flat single-colour fixture faces: dispatch desk, tea counter, exhibits counter and lab benches
findings.problem: DR-62 allows no visible flat single-colour face over 0.5 m² without trim, a panel line or a decal. The dispatch desk body is rbox(4.4,1,1.3) cream (src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:111). Its front (4.4 m²) has only five 3.5 cm rainbow stripes near the floor, and its back and ends are blank (13, 14, A2). The tea counter is rbox(2.2,.9,.62) plain pink (room.ts:111): its 2 m² front is bare (18, B3). The exhibits counter is rbox(2.6,.9,.7) plain '#e9e2d4' (room.ts:122). The lab benches are rbox(2.4,.9,.8) plain white (room.ts:96). In this white hall these slabs merge with the floor and walls and read as untextured blockout boxes next to the detailed props. They are the room's main stations, so they need the most cues (≥ 6 per fixture).
findings.fix: Dispatch desk: split the front into three panel doors (box(1.4,.7,.015) inset panels, a shade darker, with INK pull handles), add a recessed INK kick plate (box(4.3,.08,.02) at y .04) and a cable grommet + cable bundle exiting the right end toward the tower. Put the 'DISPATCH' plaque centred on the front at y .75. Tea counter: two cupboard doors with knobs, a drawer line, a white tile splash-back strip at the rear. Exhibits counter: a slatted plinth or two drawer fronts and a small engraved plaque per exhibit (UV / X-RAY / GAMMA) on the front edge, replacing the sentence on the wall. Lab benches: a drawer bank on one end, reagent shelf uprights, and a blue edge band.
findings.verify: Retake 13, 14, 18 and 42 at zoom 9. Each fixture shows ≥ 6 distinguishing cues, and no flat face over 0.5 m² is uninterrupted.
findings.verify_reason: Code: the desk is rbox(4.4,1,1.3) cream with only five 3.5 cm stripes (station.ts:111-112). The tea counter is rbox(2.2,.9,.62) plain pink (room.ts:111), the exhibits counter rbox(2.6,.9,.7) (:122), and each lab bench rbox(2.4,.9,.8) (:96). Every front face is over 2 m² with no trim. Shots 13 and 18 show large blank faces, which breaks DR-62.

findings.title: Far shell walls stay as 0.9 m lips from back and side yaws: the room shows only one tall wall when orbited
findings.problem: Only the back wall and the x = −11 side wall are built tall. The front wall (z = +8) and the x = +11 wall are permanent low lips. When the player orbits to look at the room from the back (camera at −z, A2, A5) or from the east (A3), the far walls they now face are 0.9 m rims with the dark void above. The near back wall correctly cuts away, so from those yaws the hall has no enclosing wall except x = −11. DR-75 asks that only the faces between the camera and the room drop. From the front-facing survey (A5) the room reads as a tray with one wall.
findings.fix: In the shared station room kit (RoomKit/kit.back/kit.side builder used by stations/types.ts), build all four shell walls at full 3.0 m with the same cream/rail band dressing (the rainbow rail at room.ts:57 needs front and east copies). Drive the cutaway per frame from the camera yaw: a wall drops to 0.9 m (scale.y tween) only when the dot product of its inward normal and the camera's horizontal forward vector is > 0.3. Keep the existing back/side dressing parented to the upper group so it hides with the cut.
findings.verify: Retake A2, A3 and A5 (s9-yaws.mjs). The wall facing the camera across the room is full height with the rainbow rail, and only the wall nearest the camera is a lip.
findings.verify_reason: src/levels/decor.ts:72-73 builds only the back (z−) and side (x−) as shellWall; the front and +x walls come from frontLips() (decor.ts:65) and are permanent lips. In A5 (survey from the back) only the x = −11 wall stands tall, and the z = +8 and x = +11 walls are 0.9 m rims facing the void. This breaks DR-75.
findings.fix_correction: The builder is not in stations/types.ts. It is src/levels/decor.ts: shellWall() at :32 and frontLips() at :65, called at :72-73. The per-frame cutaway already exists (game.ts:385-386 drops any shellWall whose normal·toCam > .2). So the fix is to replace frontLips with shellWall(game,l.width,0,l.depth/2,[0,1]) and shellWall(game,l.depth,l.width/2,0,[1,0]), and add the rainbow-rail copies to them in room.ts. No new cutaway logic is needed. This is shared by every level.

findings.title: Rainbow floor stripes run under the pod-dock rug and the win glow strips double up on them
findings.problem: The five wayfinding stripes are box(13.5,.006,.1) at y .008 (top .011), at z 6.9…6.26 (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:55). The pod-dock rug is a plane at y .012 spanning z 4.4…6.4 (room.ts:53, dressing.ts:24). The green stripe (z 6.21–6.31) is fully under the rug and the magenta one (6.37–6.47) is cut in half by the rug edge. The stripes are 'from the entrance' wayfinding, but they visibly disappear under the dock, and the rug and stripe surfaces are only 1 mm apart: a z-fight risk at the 38 m zoom. On the last delivery, lightUp() (room.ts:148) adds a second set of boxes, box(13.5,.01,.1) at y .014 (spanning .009–.019). These intersect the base stripes and sit above the rug at .012, so the glowing strips draw over the dock rug. The stripes also run under the clutter crates along the front.
findings.fix: Move the stripes to start after the rug: z 7.4…6.76 (6.9 + .5 − i*.16), or shorten them to x −5.0…2.85 so they start at the dock's right edge and 'lead away' from it. Make the stripes flat decal planes at y .006 (no box sides) and set the rug at y .014 with polygonOffset on the rug material. In lightUp(), don't add a second box: switch the existing stripe materials to hot(c,1.6) (keep a reference array) so there is no overlap.
findings.verify: A zoom-9 crop of the dock (s2-front.mjs shot 11) shows no stripe under the rug. Two shots 0.1 s apart while slowly orbiting at zoom 38 show no flicker at the rug edge. After the win (s6 shot 79) the glowing stripes don't overlap the rug.
findings.verify_reason: The stripes are box(13.5,.006,.1) at y .008 (top .011), at z 6.9−i*.16 (room.ts:55). The rug is at y .012 (dressing.ts:24), spanning z 4.4–6.4 and x −7.6..−5.2 (room.ts:53). The green stripe (6.21–6.31) lies entirely under the rug and the magenta stripe straddles its edge, with 1 mm of separation. lightUp boxes at y .014 ±.005 (room.ts:148) cut through the base stripes and rise above the rug. Crop 99 shows the green stripe missing under the rug and the magenta one along its edge.

findings.title: Clutter desk pod parked in front of the roof-hatch ladder; the ladder leads nowhere
findings.problem: The scene dump puts a clutter 'pod' desk (1.6×0.85) at (0.98, −6.82): it spans z −7.25…−6.40, with its monitor and chair in front. The roof-hatch ladder is at (0.9, −7.78) (src/stations/spectrum/room.ts:129). The desk and chair stand directly in front of the ladder's foot, so the bottom rungs are hidden behind a monitor and the ladder can't plausibly be used (94, 36, 37). The ladder's rails are 2.9 m on a 3.0 m wall with no hatch, opening or ceiling detail at the top, and only the wall plaque 'ROOF HATCH ↑' explains it. It reads as a ladder leaning on a blank wall.
findings.fix: Add a solid() footprint (or a clutter keep-out lane {points:[[.9,-7.6],[.9,-6.0]],r:.8}) in front of the ladder so clutter never lands there. Give the ladder a destination: a 0.9×0.9 m DMETAL hatch frame with a yellow-black hazard rim mounted on the top of the back wall at (0.9, 3.0, −7.9), its lid hinged open 30°, plus two wall brackets (box .1×.04×.12) holding the rails. Replace the 'ROOF HATCH ↑' plaque with a small arrow pictogram on the frame.
findings.verify: Rerun s8-closeups.mjs shot 94. The ladder's foot is clear for ≥ 1 m and a hatch frame is visible at the top. Rerun g.audit(.02) to confirm it still reports 0.
findings.verify_reason: The scene dump shows the clutter 'pod' desk top 1.6×0.85 at (0.98,-6.82), spanning z −7.25…−6.40, with a monitor at z −7.02. The ladder is at (0.9,-7.78) (room.ts:129), so the desk and monitor stand right in front of its foot (94). The ladder ends on a blank wall, explained only by the plaque (room.ts:130).

findings.title: Invisible bands are drawn in vivid hues everywhere (beams, stripes, rail, buttons) with no 'false colour' note
findings.problem: The room's whole decorative language is the five band colours (BANDS[].color, src/stations/spectrum/logic.ts:48-52): radio red, microwave orange, thermal orange, near-IR magenta, visible green. They appear on the floor stripes (room.ts:55), the wall rail band (:57), the desk stripes (station.ts:112) and the wall chart. The NIR beam is rendered as a hot-pink laser (65–67, 70–72) and the thermal beam as an orange laser (76–78). DR-35 says invisible bands are never shown in visible hues unless labelled 'false colour'. src/ has no 'false colour' string (grep). The bench only notes 'ribbon not to scale'. Artistically the rainbow is the room's charm, but the beam rendering teaches that near-IR is pink light.
findings.fix: Keep the decorative rainbow, but render invisible-band beams in a neutral style: a white or pale-grey dashed beam with a band-coloured end marker, only the visible band as a solid green beam. Or keep the hue and add a mounted 'FALSE COLOUR' tag on the tower turret and a 'false colour' caption next to 'ribbon not to scale' on the band monitor (station.ts monitor texture). Desaturate the IR/radio stripes to a dashed pattern in the rail band, so 'visible' is the only solid colour.
findings.verify: Retake 66 and 77 with each band selected. Only Visible shows a solid real hue; the others are neutral or carry a readable 'false colour' caption in frame. Cross-check with the spectrum-teach reviewer.
findings.verify_reason: A grep of src for 'false colour' or 'false color' finds nothing. The beam colour comes from BANDS[b].color (station.ts:268), so NIR draws as a magenta laser (66, and my verify-06) and thermal as orange (77). The ribbon, beacon and pulse are band-coloured too (station.ts:243,259,388). DR-35 is broken. P2 is acceptable for this models review; spectrum-teach may rate it higher as a teaching issue.

findings.title: Draw calls 1133 at the start view (rule ≤ ~250) and 5 point lights (rule ≤ 4)
findings.problem: snap() at start reports drawCalls 1133 at 60 fps on the host GPU (s7-audit-norim.mjs log). That is about 4.5× the DR-24 budget, so lower-end GPUs and phones will drop frames. The room has 531 meshes in the scene dump. Most of the hand-built dressing (brick slabs, shelf boards, book rows, mesh posts every 1.6 m, rainbow stripes ×5, rail bands ×10, bench keys, ladder rungs) is separate meshes rather than merged or instanced. DR-66: the room adds 5 PointLights (room.ts:144-146) where the rule allows ≤ 4.
findings.fix: Merge static decor per material once the room is dressed: BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries over decorRoot children that share a material (the same pass Lunch used to drop from 1090 to about 175). Specifically merge the stripes and rail bands into one mesh each with vertex colours, the shelf boards and stock, the ladder, the mesh posts and rails, and the brick piers. Drop the tea-corner lamp (2.4,2.4,3.8): its pool overlaps the desk lamp, and a lampPool decal can fake it.
findings.verify: snap().drawCalls ≤ 250 at the start view and in the survey. A scene traverse counts ≤ 4 PointLights, including lightUp().
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it: drawCalls 1133 without fullfx, 1137 with fullfx at start, and 1139 in the lab and survey, all at 60 fps. The scene dump lists 5 PointLights (room.ts:144-146), against DR-66's limit of 4 and the RULES 'spectrum 5'. Host fps meets DR-24, so P2 is right.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-spectrum-models/v2-dc.mjs output: spectrum fullfx=false dc 1133, fullfx=true dc 1137, lunch dc 1341
findings.fix_correction: The 'Lunch dropped from 1090 to about 175' precedent is false. My run measures Lunch at 1341 draw calls with fullfx, so no existing merge pass can be reused. Write a new merge (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries per material over static decorRoot children), and treat it as a cross-room DR-24 issue rather than a spectrum one.

findings.title: Bench view repeats values across monitor and side card; monitor microtext is below legibility
findings.problem: In the bench view (55, 57) the left monitor shows the band, λ and f, and the right monitor shows 'LINK 31.0 dB, CLEAR LINK / BLOCKED: BRICK WALL'. The right-hand HUD card lists Pod, Band, Power, Path ('blocked: brick wall') and Link margin ('31.0 dB') again. Band, path and margin are each shown twice (DR-41), and the toast repeats λ and f a third time ('Radio 100 MHz: λ = 3 m, f = 100 MHz…'). The monitor sub-captions 'c = f × λ = 3×10⁸ m/s', 'FM radio · ribbon not to scale', 'works / reliable' and 'to the storeroom' are about 6–9 px cap height at 1440×900 (DR-48 wants ≥ 14 px). Model-wise the bench itself is rich and reads well (band keys, wave ribbon between posts, tilted map lectern, two housed screens, power keys, lever and send button).
findings.fix: Drop Band, Path and Link margin from the side card (station.ts updatePanel) and keep only Pod (a status not shown elsewhere) and Power. Make the monitors the single source. Remove the λ/f toast on band change (the monitor already shows it). Enlarge the monitor captions: render the canvas so the sub-caption is ≥ 30 px on a 512 px-wide texture, or cut it to the single 'not to scale' tag.
findings.verify: Retake 55/57. No number or status appears on two panels, and every visible caption measures ≥ 14 px cap height in a crop.
findings.verify_reason: In 55, Band ('Visible 530 nm'), Path ('blocked: brick wall') and margin ('no signal') each appear on both a monitor and the side card. The band-change toast repeats λ and f (station.ts:222 say(`…λ = …, f = …`)). The monitor captions are drawn at 32 px and 24 px fonts on a 640 px canvas (station.ts:327-328), which renders at about 6–8 px cap height in 55. This breaks DR-41 and DR-48.

findings.title: Win push-in crops Pip at the frame edge and the result card covers the tower
findings.problem: The win camera (79–82) frames Pip cheering at the bottom-left. His feet are cut by the bottom edge and his left mitt reaches x ≈ 50 px (Pip spans about 11–33% of the width). The result card then covers the right 40% of the frame, including the tower, the machine that just delivered. DR-11 wants Pip and the working machine inside the centre 70%. The beam and pulse that made the moment aren't in the final frame.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts winFocus for station levels, aim at the midpoint of Pip and TX (−0.4, 1.2, 2.3) with distance about 7 and a 0.6 m lateral shift to the left of screen, so the result card (right side) covers empty floor. For spectrum, pass the last delivery pad's position as the secondary focus so the delivered pod is in frame. Keep pitch at 0.32.
findings.verify: Retake the win shots via s6-solve2.mjs. Pip's full body and the tower both sit within x 15–60% and y 15–85% of the 1440×900 frame before the card appears, and the card covers neither.
findings.verify_reason: In 79, Pip spans x of about 40–470 and is cut off at the bottom edge. In 82 the result card covers the right 40%, including the tower. winFocus for stations is table+0.5 (game.ts:398), offset 2.2 m to the right at distance 7 (game.ts:373). This breaks DR-11.
findings.fix_correction: The station win pitch is .5 (game.ts:373: pitch = this.station ? .5 : …), not .32, which is Meeting's. 'Keep pitch 0.32' would actually change it. Keep .5, or tune it deliberately. The lateral shift is already 2.2 m to camera-right, so the fix should change both the focus point (the Pip–TX midpoint) and the sign and size of that shift.

notes.models: Every distinct fixture was captured at the game camera and at zoom 9 (shots 10–44, 92–98, A6–A8, B0–B3). Works well: the brick storeroom with its wooden plank door, lintel and pier caps; the slatted lab shutter with its roller box, yellow hatch frame and sliding hatch door; the copper-mesh quiet room with real posts and rails (the see-through mesh reads instantly as a cage); the mirror boards (gradient silvered pane, both faces, lilac rail, proper stand feet); and the dispatch bench, the best model in the room (band keys with ink bezels, a wave ribbon strung between posts, a tilted map lectern, two housed screens, power keys, a lever and a send button, well past 6 cues). The coworkers (cap keeper, lab scientist, headphone reader, alarmed tea blob) read as blobs and stay on model. Weak: the transmitter tower, the room's hero object (its five band rings have a smaller radius than the mast and render inside it; it reads as a glove on a stick on a black hole); the pod (an arcade-joystick silhouette, and the lid handle runs into the mast plate); the shelf stock (bread loaves); the counters (big blank slabs); and the toaster (too small, hidden by smoke). g.audit(.02) and g.audit(.04) both report 0 overlaps at start, and the decor fixtures have solid() colliders, so the audit can see them. The overlaps that remain are logical ones the audit can't see: clutter inside beam corridors (bookshelf in the NIR beam), clutter in front of the ladder, stripes under the rug, and the handle in the pod plate.
notes.clarity: The brick, glass, metal, mesh and smoke obstacles are each distinct in material at the game camera, and the floor mirror marks (dashed lilac rings with letters) and pad rings read well. Clarity loses on colour hierarchy. Job yellow is spent on a chair and crates, while the pod and mirrors are cream, grey and lilac and blend into a hall whose floor is luma 209–233, so Pip, the held pod and the target aren't the highest-contrast shapes. Signs are single-sided floating planes: TEA hovers in air, POD DOCK stands on edge with no foot, and the QUIET ROOM sign faces into its own room, so it is invisible from the approach. The wall carries a 13-word sentence ('…exhibits only. Not safe to stand beside.'), against DR-49. In the bench view, band, path and margin are each shown on both the monitor and the side card, and the monitor captions are microtext.
notes.playability: Not my primary dimension, but noted while capturing. The survey (Tab) shows the whole room at 1440×900. Orbiting to the back or east leaves the far shell walls as 0.9 m lips (DR-75). The storeroom wall didn't fade when it hid Pip's body from a high camera (shot 14), while the same wall did fade in shot 33. The faded wall leaves its cap, piers and STOREROOM sign opaque. Draw calls are 1133 at the start view (60 fps on the host GPU), far over the ~250 budget. The level has 5 point lights. All capture scripts closed their browsers with zero console or page errors.
notes.fun: The room has charm: a rainbow research hall, a smoking toaster, a mesh Faraday cage and a mirror relay. The win moment fires confetti and a cheering Pip, but the push-in crops Pip at the bottom-left and the result card covers the tower. Model-level fun opportunities are untaken. The tower gives no visual reward (its rings are buried), the toaster smoke is a veil rather than a gag, and the pod never visibly changes state on the device except the head swap. A pod status ring and puffs that rise from the toaster would make the cause and effect of each delivery more physical.
notes.teaching: The room's lesson is that obstacles act differently per band, and the models support it well for brick, metal, mesh and glass. Two visuals undercut it. The near-IR beam is drawn passing straight through a solid bookshelf placed by clutter in the lab beam corridor (P1), and invisible bands are rendered as vivid pink and orange lasers with no 'false colour' note (DR-35). The exhibits case (UV lamp, X-ray tube, gamma pig) is a good idea, but its objects are too small and generic to read at the game camera, so the warning sentence on the wall does the teaching instead of the models.
